title: AI tools for software engineers, but without the hype – with Simon Willison (Co-Creator of Django)
summary: Simon Willison gives a grounded account of using LLMs for coding: real but uneven gains, a steep learning curve, and human judgment still in charge.

assertions.quote: you'll get this tool and it'll make you productive on day one and it absolutely won't

verdicts.note: Learning curves are real (METR's one dev with >50h Cursor experience was faster), but evidence that ramp-up reliably flips results is thin.

assertions.quote: python JavaScript they're great at rust they're not quite as good at yet

verdicts.note: Model quality tracks training-data volume; benchmarks such as MultiPL-E show much lower scores in less common languages.

assertions.quote: but that's only 10% of my job

verdicts.note: Studies of developer time show coding is a minority of work; DORA and Faros 2025 found individual coding gains often don't translate into delivery throughput.

assertions.quote: I don't think you should ever commit a line of code that a language model wrote If you don't understand it yourself

verdicts.note: Ownership and maintainability require understanding; it's a reasonable review standard rather than an empirical finding.

assertions.quote: when I combine it with these tools I will run circles around somebody who's never written a code line of code in their life

verdicts.note: Experts get more reliable results and catch errors, but several RCTs show larger measured speedups for juniors, and METR found experts slowed; contested.

assertions.quote: that means that the number of jobs of software Engineers goes up

verdicts.note: Jevons effects are historically common and plausible for software, but whether demand growth outpaces productivity for developer headcount is unproven.

assertions.quote: always tell it that you are the world's greatest expert in X before you ask all of that kind of mostly rubbish

verdicts.note: As models improved, output depends more on relevant, high-signal context than phrasing; consistent with Anthropic/Cursor guidance and long-context degradation evidence.

assertions.quote: if what we are seeing is incremental improvements like Claude 3.5 Sonet is a substantial incremental improvement over GPT 40

verdicts.note: METR's task-horizon metric kept doubling roughly every 7 months through 2025-26 and coding benchmarks rose sharply; perceived per-release gains feel smaller but the trend is steep.

assertions.quote: it's coming nobody will ever work again which helps you raise a lot of money

verdicts.note: Labs do have incentives and many evals are self-reported, but independent evals (METR, SWE-bench, LMArena) largely confirm capability gains.

assertions.quote: for adding new fact into the model it just doesn't work

verdicts.note: Studies find fine-tuning adds new facts slowly and can raise hallucination, while retrieval is the standard, better-performing way to supply fresh or private knowledge.

assertions.quote: I've actually shipped go codes to production despite not being a go programmer

verdicts.note: AI clearly lowers the barrier to unfamiliar mainstream languages, but output quality still depends on the developer's ability to judge it and drops for less common languages.
